config.title: Wittenberg Day Trip from Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Trains, tickets, the Theses Door and what the Lutherhaus closure changes.

items.q: How do I get from Berlin to Wittenberg by train?
items.a: **Take the ICE from Berlin Hauptbahnhof, about 41 minutes, roughly hourly**, or the RE3 regional train, 1 hour 27 minutes, about every two hours, which also stops at Potsdamer Platz and Südkreuz. Both arrive at Lutherstadt Wittenberg Hbf, a 12 minute walk from the old town. Times checked on 4 September 2026.

items.q: Is the Deutschlandticket valid to Wittenberg?
items.a: **Yes, on the RE3 regional train the 63 euro Deutschlandticket covers the whole trip.** It is never valid on the ICE. The Brandenburg-Berlin-Ticket does not work at all here, because Wittenberg lies in Saxony-Anhalt, outside that ticket's area.

items.q: Is the Lutherhaus in Wittenberg open?
items.a: **No. The Lutherhaus is closed for renovation until spring 2027.** The museum shows its key pieces in the Augusteum next door as the exhibition Literally Luther, daily 10:00 to 18:00, 6 euros, reduced 4, scheduled until early January 2027.

items.q: Can you see the door where Luther posted the 95 theses?
items.a: **You see the place, with a later door.** The wooden door of 1517 burned in 1760; since 1858 a bronze door with the full Latin text of the theses stands in the same portal of the Castle Church. Entry costs a 3 euro preservation fee, and Luther's grave is inside.

items.q: How many hours do you need in Wittenberg?
items.a: **Five to six hours in town covers everything comfortably**: the walk in past the Luther oak, the Augusteum exhibition, lunch on the market square, the Town Church with the Cranach altar, and the Castle Church with the tower climb before the 16:00 last ascent.

items.q: Is a Wittenberg day trip worth it on a Monday?
items.a: **Yes, with one gap: the Melanchthonhaus closes on Mondays.** Both churches and the Augusteum exhibition stay open. If you want every museum, pick another weekday; if you mainly want the churches, the door and the town itself, Monday works fine.
